name: Chloracantha

project_scope.note: C. spinosa is a high-priority live source concept but is not currently installed in data/manifest.json. This genus lesson is recognition scaffolding only and does not promote the species.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Ignore the flower first and look at the plant skeleton: erect green photosynthetic stems arise from rhizomes, leaves are alternate but drop early, and sharply ascending side branches can be reduced to thorn-like tips. Then confirm small daisy-like heads with white rays and yellow disks.
priority: alternate narrow leaves present mainly on young growth and early deciduous

quick_split: C. spinosa — coarse, rhizomatous, often nearly leafless perennial/subshrub; green broom-like stems and sharply ascending branches are the fastest habit cue.
Young growth can carry narrow oblanceolate leaves, but mature flowering plants may look almost leafless because those leaves are early deciduous.
Do not require every branch to be thorny: some lateral branches become thorns, but thorn expression is variable.
comparison_lesson.family_context: The white-rayed heads confirm Asteraceae, but the combination of persistent green photosynthetic stems, ephemeral leaves, rhizomatous colonies, and occasional thorn-like branches is the stronger field-recognition package.

visual_needs: whole colony showing rhizomatous clumping and erect green broom-like stems
whole flowering stem showing the nearly leafless mature architecture
young stem with alternate narrow leaves before they drop
closeup of a lateral branch modified into a thorn
closeup of a white-rayed yellow-disk head and involucre
annotated comparison showing ordinary ascending branch versus thorn-modified branch
source_notes: Nesom's Chloracantha treatment describes rhizomatous perennial subshrubs with erect green stems, sharply ascending lateral branches sometimes modified as thorns, alternate early-deciduous leaves, and radiate heads.
Texas A&M's Texas rangeland treatment independently emphasizes green striped stems, brief spring foliage, rhizomatous colonies, occasional spines, and white rays with yellow disks.
